The curve $$C$$ has equation $$y=x(x-1)(x+2)$$. The shaded areas above and below the $$x$$-axis are equal. Show that the $$x$$-coordinate of $$A$$ satisfies $$(x-1)^2(3x^2+10x+5)=0.$$
Chapter 13- Integration.hint: Let $$x=a<0$$ be the $$x$$-coordinate of $$A$$, equate the positive area from $$a$$ to $$0$$ with the magnitude of the negative area from $$0$$ to $$1$$ and simplify.
Chapter 13- Integration.solution_text: $$y=x(x-1)(x+2)=x^3+x^2-2x$$ $$\int_{a}^{0}y\,dx=-\int_{0}^{1}y\,dx$$ $$-\left[\tfrac14 x^4+\tfrac13 x^3-x^2\right]_{a}^{0}=-\left[\tfrac14 x^4+\tfrac13 x^3-x^2\right]_{0}^{1}$$ $$-\left(0-\tfrac14 a^4-\tfrac13 a^3+a^2\right)=-\left(\tfrac14+\tfrac13-1\right)$$ $$-\tfrac14 a^4-\tfrac13 a^3+a^2=\tfrac{5}{12}\Rightarrow3a^4+4a^3-12a^2+5=0$$ $$\Rightarrow (a-1)^2(3a^2+10a+5)=0.$$

Chapter 13- Integration.question_title: Coordinates of A and other roots

Chapter 13- Integration.solution_text: $$(x-1)^2(3x^2+10x+5)=0\Rightarrow x=1\ (\text{double root})\text{ or }x=\frac{-10\pm\sqrt{40}}{6}=\frac{-5\pm\sqrt{10}}{3}$$ $$A\text{ lies between }-2\text{ and }0\Rightarrow x_A=\frac{-5+\sqrt{10}}{3}$$ $$y_A=x_A(x_A-1)(x_A+2)=-\frac{80}{27}+\frac{37\sqrt{10}}{27}$$ $$\Rightarrow A\left(\tfrac{-5+\sqrt{10}}{3},\,-\tfrac{80}{27}+\tfrac{37\sqrt{10}}{27}\right)$$ $$x=1\text{ is the }x\text{-coordinate of }B\text{ where }C\text{ crosses the }x\text{-axis, and }x=\tfrac{-5-\sqrt{10}}{3}\text{ gives another point to the left where the positive and negative areas would again be equal if that part of }C\text{ were included.}$$

Chapter 13- Integration.solution_text: $$-x^2-2x+3=x+3\Rightarrow -x^2-3x=0\Rightarrow x=0,-3$$; on $$[-3,0]$$ the curve is above the line, so $$A=\int_{-3}^{0}\left[(-x^2-2x+3)-(x+3)\right]dx=\int_{-3}^{0}(-x^2-3x)dx=\left[-\tfrac13 x^3-\tfrac32 x^2\right]_{-3}^{0}=\tfrac{9}{2}.$$

The curve has equation $$y=x^2+1$$ and the line has equation $$y=7-x$$. The finite region $$R_1$$ is bounded by the line, the curve and the $$y$$-axis as shown. Find the area of $$R_1$$.
Chapter 13- Integration.hint: Find where line and curve meet, then integrate $$y_{\text{line}}-y_{\text{curve}}$$ from the left intersection to the $$y$$-axis.
Chapter 13- Integration.solution_text: $$x^2+1=7-x\Rightarrow x^2+x-6=0\Rightarrow(x+3)(x-2)=0\Rightarrow x=-3,2$$ On $$[-3,0]$$ the line is above the curve, so $$A_{R_1}=\int_{-3}^{0}\big[(7-x)-(x^2+1)\big]\,dx=\int_{-3}^{0}(6-x-x^2)\,dx$$ $$=\left[6x-\tfrac12 x^2-\tfrac13 x^3\right]_{-3}^{0}=0-\left(-18-\tfrac92+9\right)=\tfrac{27}{2}$$ $$\text{Area of }R_1=\tfrac{27}{2}\ \text{square units}$$

Chapter 13- Integration.question_text: The curve has equation $$y=\dfrac{2}{x^2}+x$$. Points $$A$$ and $$B$$ on the curve have $$x$$-coordinates $$\tfrac12$$ and $$2$$ respectively. Find the area of the finite region between chord $$AB$$ and the curve.
Chapter 13- Integration.hint: Find coordinates of $$A,B$$, the equation of chord $$AB$$, then integrate $$y_{\text{line}}-y_{\text{curve}}$$ from $$x=\tfrac12$$ to $$x=2$$.
Chapter 13- Integration.solution_text: For $$x=\tfrac12$$, $$y_A=\dfrac{2}{(1/2)^2}+\tfrac12=8+\tfrac12=\tfrac{17}{2}$$; for $$x=2$$, $$y_B=\dfrac{2}{4}+2=\tfrac12+2=\tfrac52$$. Slope $$m=\dfrac{5/2-17/2}{2-1/2}=-4$$ so line $$AB$$ is $$y-5/2=-4(x-2)\Rightarrow y=-4x+\tfrac{21}{2}$$. Then $$A=\int_{1/2}^{2}\big((-4x+\tfrac{21}{2})-(\dfrac{2}{x^2}+x)\big)\,dx=\int_{1/2}^{2}\left(-5x+\tfrac{21}{2}-\dfrac{2}{x^2}\right)dx$$ $$=\left[-\tfrac{5}{2}x^2+\tfrac{21}{2}x+2x^{-1}\right]_{1/2}^{2}=\tfrac{27}{8}$$ $$\text{Area between }AB\text{ and the curve}=\tfrac{27}{8}\ \text{square units}$$

Chapter 13- Integration.question_text: The curve has equation $$y=3\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{x^3}+4$$ and the line has equation $$y=4-\tfrac12 x$$. Verify that the line and the curve cross at the point $$A(4,2)$$.
Chapter 13- Integration.hint: Substitute $$x=4$$ into both equations and compare the resulting $$y$$ values.
Chapter 13- Integration.solution_text: For the curve: $$y=3\sqrt{4}-\sqrt{4^3}+4=3\cdot2-\sqrt{64}+4=6-8+4=2$$. For the line: $$y=4-\tfrac12\cdot4=4-2=2$$. Thus both give $$y=2$$, so $$A(4,2)$$ is a point of intersection.

Chapter 13- Integration.question_text: For the curve $$y=3\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{x^3}+4$$ and the line $$y=4-\tfrac12 x$$, find the area of the finite region bounded by the curve and the line.
Chapter 13- Integration.hint: Find both intersection points (at $$x=0$$ and $$x=4$$) and integrate $$y_{\text{curve}}-y_{\text{line}}$$ from $$0$$ to $$4$$.
Chapter 13- Integration.solution_text: Setting $$3\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{x^3}+4=4-\tfrac12 x$$ gives $$3\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{x^3}+\tfrac12 x=0$$. With substitution $$t=\sqrt{x}$$ this becomes $$t(3-t^2+\tfrac12 t^2)=t(3-\tfrac12 t^2)=0$$ so $$t=0$$ or $$t=\sqrt{6}$$; hence $$x=0,6$$, but only the portion shown is from $$x=0$$ to $$x=4$$ where the region is finite, bounded by the two curves. The area is $$A=\int_{0}^{4}\big(3\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{x^3}+4-(4-\tfrac12 x)\big)\,dx=\int_{0}^{4}\left(3x^{1/2}-x^{3/2}+\tfrac12 x\right)dx$$ $$=\left[2x^{3/2}-\tfrac{2}{5}x^{5/2}+\tfrac14 x^2\right]_{0}^{4}=2\cdot8-\tfrac{2}{5}\cdot32+\tfrac14\cdot16=\tfrac{36}{5}$$ $$\text{Area of the finite region}=\tfrac{36}{5}\ \text{square units}$$

Chapter 13- Integration.question_text: The curve has equation $$y=p+10x-x^2$$ and the line has equation $$y=qx+25$$. The line cuts the curve at points $$A$$ and $$B$$ with $$x$$-coordinates $$4$$ and $$8$$ respectively. Show that $$p=-7$$ and calculate the value of $$q$$.
Chapter 13- Integration.hint: Use equality of $$y$$-values at $$x=4$$ and $$x=8$$ to form two equations in $$p,q$$, then solve simultaneously.
Chapter 13- Integration.solution_text: At $$x=4$$: $$p+10\cdot4-4^2=p+24=4q+25.$$ At $$x=8$$: $$p+10\cdot8-8^2=p+16=8q+25.$$ Subtracting gives $$(p+16)-(p+24)=(8q+25)-(4q+25)\Rightarrow-8=4q\Rightarrow q=-2.$$ Substituting into $$p+24=4q+25$$ gives $$p+24=-8+25=17\Rightarrow p=-7.$$

Chapter 13- Integration.question_text: The line through $$A$$ parallel to the $$x$$-axis meets the curve again at point $$C$$. Calculate the coordinates of $$C$$.

Chapter 13- Integration.solution_text: With $$p=-7$$, at $$x=4$$ we have $$y_A=-7+40-16=17,$$ so line $$AC$$ has equation $$y=17.$$ Solve $$-7+10x-x^2=17\Rightarrow-x^2+10x-24=0\Rightarrow x^2-10x+24=0\Rightarrow(x-4)(x-6)=0,$$ so the other intersection is at $$x=6$$. Thus $$C=(6,17).$$

Chapter 13- Integration.solution_text: Area $$A=\int_{4}^{6}\big((-7+10x-x^2)-17\big)dx=\int_{4}^{6}(-x^2+10x-24)\,dx=\left(-\tfrac13 x^3+5x^2-24x\right)_{4}^{6}$$ $$=\left(-72+180-144\right)-\left(-\tfrac{64}{3}+80-96\right)=(-36)-\left(-\tfrac{112}{3}\right)=\tfrac{4}{3}.$$So the shaded area is $$\tfrac{4}{3}$$ square units.
